title: Predicted vs actual commando calibration ledger
desc: Orchestration discipline: before dispatching an agent, record the PREDICTED outcome + foreseen risk; after it returns, record the ROOT-VERIFIED ACTUAL; the delta is the calibration/learning signal. Knowledge-ify in advance, fill actuals as agents land. Worked example = the 2026-06-19 modular pre-tool harness refactor.
steps: DISCIPLINE: before dispatching any agent/commando, WRITE the PREDICTED outcome (pass/fail, expected result, the KEY RISK you foresee). After it returns, record the ACTUAL -- ROOT-verified, not the agent self-report (an agent summary is intent, not proof). The DELTA between predicted and actual is the learning signal: a predicted risk that MATERIALIZES validates your risk-sense; a SURPRISE marks a knowledge gap to capture. Keep a ledger per multi-agent campaign; knowledge-ify the methodology + predictions IN ADVANCE, fill actuals as agents land.

WHY: forecasting before dispatch forces explicit risk-modeling instead of blind delegation; the recorded delta makes orchestration self-improving (next campaign's predictions are calibrated by this one). Pairs with wkhippo foresee (predecessor outcomes) and verify-don't-trust (the ledger ACTUAL must be ROOT-verified live, never the agent claim).

METHODOLOGY captured (this campaign): design-dialogue -> capture each rule into spec skill -> Plan agent maps current-to-target + risks -> wksplit bake-off (is a 0-token deterministic split even applicable?) -> per-module commandos build proto + self-test GREEN standalone (test-first) -> ROOT promotes -proto and wires into heart registry LAST (wire-last) -> live re-verify each merge.

LEDGER 2026-06-19 modular harness refactor (PRED -> ACT): wksplit bake-off PRED 0-token-but-likely-struggles-on-inline-heavy -> ACT FAIL (only 2 functions found, G5 run-verify fail on dot-source deps) = hypothesis disproven, wksplit fits function-heavy pure-shard only. M1 decompose PRED green -> ACT 23/23 green (match). M2 willkim PRED green -> ACT 30/30 at 99ms (match + sub-1s confirmed). M3 skillcheck PRED green+anti-false-positive -> ACT 15/15 anchor verified (match). S2 write-target PRED resolver+sentinel -> ACT 52/52 +UNRESOLVED sentinel (match). S1 brief-guard PRED 4/4 surgical-merge -> ACT 4/4 surgical (match, surgical predicted correctly). S3 classifier-final PRED green+flagged-live-blast-radius -> ACT 82/82 sandbox BUT live-verify caught a 2-to-dev-null regression = predicted RISK MATERIALIZED, verify-don't-trust paid off. fix2 stderr PRED logic-hole -> ACT 84/84 but root was missing-test-coverage (logic already correct) = SURPRISE, the bug was soft-Block+coverage not logic. Plan agent PRED refactor-map -> ACT A-grade 9-risk plan EXCEEDING (surfaced R7 guards-infra-needs-wksplit + R5 pre-allow-sentinel I had not anticipated). nonce P PRED 6/6+self-spawn-intact -> ACT 6/6 self-spawn intact (match). M4/M5 PRED green -> ACT pending. ROOT wire-last PRED registry+watchdog, risk=.md pre-allow ordering + Start-Job overhead -> ACT pending.

KEY CALIBRATION LESSONS: (1) a flagged live-risk that materializes (S3) is a WIN for the process, not a failure -- it proves live-verify-over-sandbox-trust earns its cost. (2) a SURPRISE (fix2: assumed logic-bug, was coverage-gap) is the highest-value ledger entry -- capture it. (3) delegation can EXCEED prediction (Plan surfaced unforeseen risks) -- do not under-scope an architect agent. (4) a disproven hypothesis (wksplit) is cheap knowledge when you bake-off empirically instead of arguing.

RELATION TO EXISTING SKILLS (this EXTENDS, does not duplicate -- CONSULT these FIRST per senior-session-first-lookup): the parallel-commando + knowledge-ify-during-wait orchestration is already fully specified in orchestrate-sectors-parallel-while-knowledgeifying -- USE IT, including its step-9 directive to FAVOR other-family executors (wkgpt/wkgemini/wkcodex, which are pace-exempt and save the scarce Anthropic Claude budget); authoring a whole module-build campaign on Claude sonnet Agents (as happened 2026-06-19) was a BUDGET MISS the existing skill already warned against. The verify-the-ACTUAL methodology is verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static (synthetic for logic / live for behavior / static for structure; structural validity is NEVER runtime correctness; every guard ships a does-it-actually-fire canary) -- its step 4 already named the 'guard present but silently not firing' fail-open class, which is exactly the soft-Block-exit-1 toothlessness rediscovered 2026-06-19. The calibration concept overlaps pace-calibration-log (which logs pace anchors). NET-NEW value of THIS skill = only the per-dispatch predicted-vs-actual LEDGER FORMAT + the four calibration lessons; everything else, search and read the existing skills IN FULL before authoring. META-LESSON: careless/ truncated skill reading (head -N, no skill search) causes reinvention of existing policy -- search-first, read-in-full.

LEDGER ACTUALS FILLED 2026-06-19: M4 multiread PRED green -> ACT 48/48 + found-and-fixed a sed-omission bug (match, bonus). M5 singlewrite PRED green -> ACT 28/28 (match). wkcodex wire-build PRED green -> ACT FALSE-SUCCESS: exit 0 but ZERO files created (the documented rc=0 codex false-success class). Caught by ROOT-verify checking the actual files exist; switched executor per orchestrate step 5, did NOT 3rd-retry. Sonnet wire-build PRED green + flagged-.md-ordering-risk -> ACT 15/15 integration GREEN, ROOT-verified by re-running the test myself; BUT ROOT-verify ALSO caught that study-lock was NOT wired and the test .md->allow case PASSED without ever exercising study-lock (a coverage GLOSS, same class as fix2) -> NOT live-mergeable, spawned a study-lock-integration increment. STRONGEST CALIBRATION LESSON of this campaign: a PASSING test is not proof the REQUIREMENT is met -- the Sonnet test reported 15/15 yet silently failed to check its own stated study-lock requirement. ROOT-verify is therefore TWO LAYERS: (a) RUN the test yourself (catches rc=0 false-success like wkcodex), AND (b) READ what each assertion actually asserts (catches a green test that glosses the real requirement). Both failure modes bit this campaign; both were caught ONLY by ROOT looking, NEVER by the agent self-report. Pair with verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static.

CUTOVER CYCLE OUTCOME 2026-06-20 (the campaign climax -- strongest calibration entry): heart-v2 live cutover PRED green + REPEATEDLY-flagged false-positive-block risk (I warned the fail-safe catches exceptions but NOT a wrong-but-valid verdict). ACT: the predicted risk MATERIALIZED on the FIRST live command -- git -C path rev-parse (a read) was false-BLOCKED by singlewrite (git global-flag -C broke the subcommand match). RECOVERY (the whole safety apparatus working end-to-end): kill-switch (.heart-v2-off) reverted INSTANTLY, zero brick, zero lockout (validated the entry-indirection+killswitch+fail-safe cutover design); then a BUG-audit commando found 12 coverage-gap bugs of the same class (2 false-block + 6 false-allow + 4 fast-path); a consolidated fix commando fixed them (86/86 corpus + 95/95 KC, no regression); ROOT 2-layer-verified (ran + read assertions); promoted the 4 fixed modules; re-verified (83/83 + real-mode + git -C rev-parse now ALLOW); removed kill-switch; re-cutover; LIVE-SMOKE git -C rev-parse = allow, git status = allow, no brick = SUCCESS. LESSON: a flagged risk that MATERIALIZES is the process WORKING, not failing -- because the safety net (kill-switch + bug-hunt + 2-layer-verify) was built for exactly that, it contained + fixed + re-delivered with zero harm. The cost of building the kill-switch was repaid in full the moment the cutover hit the predicted false-block. Build the revert BEFORE the risky change, always.

AK LIVE-WIRE FAIL-OPEN CYCLE 2026-06-20 (a NEW failure mode -- caught + reverted): the anti-knowledge guard live-wire (wkharness.ps1 insertion) PRED green (28/28 synthetic smoke, ROOT-run). ACT: on live promote it FAIL-OPENED THE WHOLE HARNESS -- knowledge-op-pipe AND anti-knowledge commands (git -c core.hooksPath, skill read piped to head) all ran UNGATED = a security hole, WORSE than a brick. Caught only by LIVE-smoke (running real commands through the PROMOTED harness, NOT the synthetic smoke which passed). Reverted instantly to the heart-v2-redirect known-good; enforcement restored (pipe blocks again). ROOT-CAUSES (3): (a) the AK module dot-source was Test-Path-guarded but NOT try/catch-guarded -> a live load error aborts the hook script -> fail-open everything; (b) Block was called with -Hard, a param REMOVED earlier the SAME campaign -> throws -> caught -> AK-match fail-opens; (c) likely trigger: the AK module emits STDOUT at load, polluting the PreToolUse decision JSON -> mis-parse -> fail-open. LESSONS: (1) a PreToolUse hook must emit ZERO stdout except its decision -- any stray load-time stdout fail-opens the gate; (2) any top-level dot-source in a live gate MUST be try/catch wrapped (a load error must never abort the hook); (3) SYNTHETIC SMOKE IS INSUFFICIENT for a live-gate wire -- 28/28 simulated-JSON passed while the LIVE hook fail-opened; a live-gate change needs a LIVE-smoke (real command through the promoted harness) PLUS a zero-stdout-at-load assertion; (4) a leftover removed-param throws silently into a fail-open catch. The fail-OPEN (not brick) was INVISIBLE to synthetic verification -- only live-smoke + the known-good revert contained it. Build the revert + the live-smoke BEFORE wiring a live gate.
